tlingit_gonakadet: Swanton's Wrangell narrative derives the Gonakadet from an unnamed human hunter, and his wife and daughters became the unnamed collective creek-women rather than individuated figures, leaving no citable genealogical tie to any registry figure (Swanton 1909).
tlingit_tlanaxeedakw: Ethnographies describe the Wealth Woman as a solitary forest apparition carrying a nameless infant and record no kinship between her and any other individuated Tlingit being (de Laguna 1972; McClellan 1963).
tlingit_natsilane: The killer-whale maker acts alone in clan tradition; his brothers-in-law and the whales he carved remain unnamed in the sources, so no attested relation to another registered figure exists (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
tlingit_duktootl: The Strong Man's uncle, kinsfolk, and the sea lions of his feat are unnamed in the recorded versions, leaving Blackskin without documented links to other individuated figures (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
tlingit_kaats: Kaats''s bear wife and bear children are unnamed in the recorded tellings, so no cited relation to another individuated figure can be registered (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
toraja_pong_lalondong: Attested across the scholarship as the cock-lord who rules, guards and judges the dead in Puya, but with no parentage or marriage recorded for him in the liturgical god-genealogies (Nooy-Palm, The Sa'dan-Toraja I, 1979; Van der Veen, The Sa'dan Toradja Chant for the Deceased, 1966).
toraja_indo_belo_tumbang: Named in the scholarship only as the goddess of curative medicine invoked in the maro ritual, with no genealogy or consort recorded ('Toraja Religion', The Encyclopedia of Religion, vol. 14, 1987; Nooy-Palm, The Sa'dan-Toraja II, 1986).
wayuu_ulepala: Ulepala is remembered as a solitary legendary man whose myth records no attested parentage or kin, only his lone journey to the land of the dead (Perrin 1976).
wik_mungkan_kapa: Kapa the Moon is an independent celestial pulwaiya with its own origin story and totemic site, recorded without any attested genealogical tie to other Munkan ancestors (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_min_monti: Min Monti the jabiru is a self-standing clan totem centred on its own increase-site (auwa), with no attested kinship to other pulwaiya (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_min_wuka: Min Wuka the flying-fox is an independent clan pulwaiya with its own myth and increase-site, recorded without attested genealogical links (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_kongkong: Kongkong the white fish-hawk is a self-standing totemic ancestor tied to the origin of the fishing-net and its own site, with no attested kinship to other pulwaiya (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
yapese_lug: Müller records Lug (Lugalang) as one of the two great Yapese sky gods beside Yalafath, but the tradition transmits him without attested parentage or named divine associates; in afterlife belief he devours the soul-that-dies together with an unnamed friend.
aymara_ekeko: Colonial and archaeological sources present Ekeko as an independent household god of abundance with no attested divine parentage, consort or sibling (Ponce Sanginés, Tunupa y Ekako, 1969).
aymara_wari: Bouysse-Cassagne describes Wari as a primordial, autochthonous chthonic power of the world below whose myths give him no attested lineage or partner (Bouysse-Cassagne, Lluvias y cenizas, 1988).
bai_li_mi: Li Mi entered Bai religion as a defeated Tang enemy general propitiated at the General's Cave, standing outside the genealogy of the Nanzhao-Dali pantheon with no attested kin or divine peers.
bai_xinuluo: Xinuluo is venerated as a self-standing founding ancestor and mountain lord of Weibaoshan whose recorded kin (father Jiadupang, grandfather Shelong) are not themselves individuated benzhu in this corpus.
berber_bonchor: Bonchor stands at the centre of the Dii Mauri relief from Vaga, but the registry does not yet contain the other six Moorish gods (Macurgum, Matilam, Vihinam, Varsissima, Macurtam, Iunam) with whom he formed that local pantheon, so no in-set relation is available (Camps 1954).
berber_aulisua: Aulisua is attested only by isolated Latin dedications naming him as deus sanctus, with no genealogy or divine associate recorded in the sources (Benabou 1976).
berber_ieru: Ieru is known solely from a single Numidian rock inscription with a radiate head, which records no kin or companion deity (Camps, Encyclopedie berbere, s.v. 'Ieru').
berber_bacax: Bacax is documented only by the dated cave dedications of Thibilis, which attach no consort, parent, or fellow deity to him (Camps, Encyclopedie berbere, vol. 9, 1991).
bicolano_bakunawa: Bakunawa is recorded in the Bicol lexicon of Marcos de Lisboa purely as the cosmic serpent that swallows the moon during eclipses, with no attested genealogical or narrative link to the Gugurang-Asuang pantheon or the Ibalong heroes.
choctaw_nalusa_chito: Choctaw sources describe Nalusa Chito / Impa Shilup as a solitary predatory shadow-being with no recorded parentage, offspring, or spouse; he acts alone upon vulnerable individuals (Swanton 1931; Mould 2004).
choctaw_bohpoli: Bohpoli / Kowi Anukasha is depicted as a small man who 'lived alone in the woods' and let himself be seen by no one, with no attested kin among the wider Choctaw pantheon (Bushnell 1909; Swanton 1931).
choctaw_hoklonoteshe: Hoklonote'she appears in the ethnographic record as an isolated shape-shifting spirit defined by its powers rather than by any family or alliance (Swanton 1931).
choctaw_ishkitini: Ishkitini is recorded as an independent night-prowling owl-being and death omen without documented genealogy or relations to other figures (Swanton 1931; Bushnell 1909).
dine_coyote: Coyote (Mąʼii / Áłtsé Hashké) is a boundary-crossing trickster whose defining role is to stand apart from and disrupt the ordered company of the Holy People rather than to be fixed in stable kinship or alliance with any one of them (Haile, Navajo Coyote Tales, 1984; Luckert, Coyoteway, 1979).
embera_ba: Ba, the Thunder, is named only as one of the beings that co-inhabit the upper world (bajía) with Karagabí, with no attested genealogy or personal relationship of its own (Bioetnia 2011).
evenki_agdy: Agdy, the personified thunder and its iron thunder-birds, is tied in Evenki belief to individual shamans and to the thunder-ancestors of the lower world rather than descended within the sky-god's lineage, and the sources document it as standing apart from the creator genealogy (Vasilevich 1969; Ol'khovatov 2023).
haida_property_woman: She is a self-standing wealth-spirit encountered in the forest and along the shore, with no genealogy or fixed partner attested in Swanton's or Barbeau's records.
haida_konankada: The Chief of the Undersea World is depicted as an independent sovereign of the sea-realm, without attested parentage or spouse in the Haida sources.
haida_nanasimgit: He is the hero of a self-contained rescue narrative whose only named relative, his wife Ḵ'uljáad, is not otherwise an individuated figure of the pantheon.
huichol_kieri: Kieri stands apart as the solitary malevolent plant-sorcerer and adversary of the deer culture-hero, not a member of the ancestral 'Our Mothers/Fathers' family, and the sources give him no attested parentage (Furst & Myerhoff 1966; Knab 1977).
huichol_haramara: Tatéi Haramara is the independent divine personification of the Pacific Ocean venerated at the western sacred site of San Blas, presented in the sources as a primeval water-mother without fixed divine parentage (Lumholtz 1900; Schaefer & Furst 1996).
huichol_niwetsika: Tatéi Niwetsika is the maize-mother whose five daughters are the coloured corn-maidens; the sources present her as an autonomous 'Our Mother' ancestor-deity of sustenance without a fixed divine parentage (Zingg 1938; Myerhoff 1974).
ijaw_bouakarakarabiri: As an independent forest wizard he stands outside the Orua lineages, dispensing invulnerability-charms to hero and rival alike rather than belonging to either family.
ket_kaigus: The forest-master Kaigus is documented as an independent owner-spirit of the taiga with no attested genealogy or myth-kinship to the cosmic deities, standing alone among the Ket masters of nature (Alekseenko 1967).
ket_kholai: Kholai is recorded only as the free-standing mistress of the hunted animals, without cited parentage or narrative ties to other Ket figures (Alekseenko 1967; Vajda 2011).
ket_ulgys: Ulgys is attested solely as the autonomous owner of the rivers and their fish, with no genealogical or relational links to the sky-god or other beings in the sources (Alekseenko 1967; Vajda 2011).
khmer_preah_pisnukar: The divine architect of the Poem of Angkor Wat acts alone as Indra's sent craftsman and has no attested kin or peer within the Khmer founder-pantheon (Jacob 1996).
khmer_preah_thorani: The Buddhist earth goddess is a self-standing cosmic witness with no attested genealogy or peer relationship in the Khmer record, defined solely by her role beneath the Buddha's throne (Guthrie 2004).
khmer_yeay_mao: As an individuated local tutelary spirit she stands as her own named cult without attested kinship or partnership to the other figures of the Khmer pantheon (Ang Choulean 1986).
kirati_nahangma: Nahangma stands apart as the martial mountaintop deity of the Nahangma rite whose one narrative tie is an antagonism with the grandmother-goddess Yuma; because that bond is a symmetric opposition with a pre-existing figure it is described in prose rather than wired, leaving her without an attested genealogical parent or directed link.
klamath_llao: Llao's defining bond is his adversarial relationship with the above-world chief Skell, expressed narratively in the Crater Lake origin story rather than through any attested kinship, parentage, or subordination tie recordable as a directed relation (Clark 1953; Deur 2008).
kondh_niyam_raja: As the supreme god-king and mythic ancestor of the Dongria Kondh sub-group, Niyam Raja heads his own Niyamgiri cosmology and is not attested with a genealogical tie to the plains-Kondh Bura Pennu pantheon.
kondh_nirantali: Nirantali is the self-standing creatrix of the distinct Kuttia Kondh cosmogony and is not documented as child, consort or subordinate of the Bura Pennu and Tari Pennu creation account.
